label: <DEL> step of short sequences (L<=5), favored by first token t/s/d and last token j/y/b/3/h/e
explanation: Fires only on the delimiter step (t == L, input <DEL>), never during the original or copy phases. It is limited to short sequences: about 82% of activation mass is at L = 3-4, about 17% at L = 5, a trace at L = 6, and none at L >= 7. Within that, which tokens appeared shapes it in a graded way that looks additive. The first token matters (t, s, d give the highest rates and together carry about 63% of mass), and so does the last original token (j strongest, then 3, y, b, h, e). Sequences with fewer digits fire more often. The top activations, such as s u u y and t u j y, combine an s/t start with a j/y ending. Precision of phase==1 alone is 0.4%, so the token content is essential, but no clean boolean captures it: the best predicate gets about 0.26 precision and 0.40 recall (dev F1 0.32, mass recall 0.53). It covers the high-activation quartile better (62%) than the low one (22%).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=j (+3.61), prev_tok=3 (+3.39), phase=1 & out_tok=t (+3.14), phase=1 & out_tok=d (+2.89), phase=1 & out_tok=s (+2.55), prev_tok=h (+2.53). Lower it: in_first=0 (-3.01), in_count=1 (-2.31), orig1=l (-1.93), recall_idx=-1 (-1.27).
